rationales.wacc: 10.5%. This is analyst judgment; the snapshot has no beta, risk-free rate or credit spread. Micron is a commodity-memory manufacturer whose revenue and margins swing hard across the cycle. FY2025 FCF margin was about 4.5% and FY2026 about 44.3% (see fcf_margin). That cyclicality calls for an equity risk premium above the semiconductor average. Debt is small ($5.179B total debt including finance leases, S-0a86662e54, against $38.364B cash, F-455b2cbdf8), so WACC is effectively the cost of equity. 10.5% sits inside the gate band [6%, 16%] and above the roughly 9-10% one would use for a less cyclical large-cap semiconductor. No precise market-implied input was available to calibrate it.
rationales.terminal_growth: 3.0%: long-run nominal growth for a memory supplier whose bit demand is tied to data-center/AI and device content growth [Q-7, Q-8]. It is held at about nominal GDP rather than above it because memory pricing mean-reverts and the business is capital-intensive. The terminal value starts from a year-5 revenue level that has already been normalized below peak (see revenue_growth) and a mid-cycle FCF margin of 30%. Within the gate band [0, 4%].
rationales.revenue_growth: Year 1 (NTM) revenue is set by code from assumptions.json: about $269.5B, anchored on the FQ1-27 guidance of $61.5B [Q-1]. Years 2-5 are +5%, -10%, -15%, -5%. This is analyst judgment for a cycle peak followed by normalization. Year 2 is still positive because demand exceeds industry supply [Q-7, Q-8], management expects a stronger FY2027 [Q-6], and strategic customer agreements with price bands are in place [Q-9, Q-12]. Years 3-5 assume supply catches up and pricing falls toward the price-band floors. Memory has always mean-reverted after supply-constrained peaks. Even after the decline, year-5 revenue (about $206B) stays well above FY2026's $133.2B because of the higher price floors [Q-9]. Downside from export restrictions [Q-11] is not modeled separately.
rationales.fcf_margin: Years 1-5: 55%, 50%, 42%, 35%, 30%. Grounding: FCF = CFO (mapped NetCashProvidedByUsedInOperatingActivities) minus capex (PaymentsToAcquirePropertyPlantAndEquipment), divided by revenue, all from `eu.py history`. FY2025: CFO $17.525B less capex $15.857B on revenue $37.378B = 4.5%. FY2026: CFO $89.675B less capex $30.712B on revenue $133.188B = 44.3%. FY2026 by quarter: Q1 22.1% (F-e8854ed703, F-f322f0ab0e, F-b11cd8f3c2); Q2 23.1%; Q3 42.4% (D-0a072dc8dc, D-dc2ab297af, F-03e050e3a0); Q4 60.6% (D-21b02a031c, D-17b54bd7f0, D-e90aac72b9; a 14-week quarter [Q-10]). Year 1 at 55% is set a little below the latest quarter's 60.6%. The NTM operating margin implied by assumptions.json is about 82% (85.95% GM less 3.76% opex), but capex is assumed to keep rising with the supply build-out (FY2026 capex was 23% of revenue) and working capital absorbs cash as revenue grows. Margins then fall with pricing in years 3-5. The 30% terminal margin is below the two-year pooled FY2025-FY2026 FCF margin of 35.5% ($60.6B FCF on $170.6B revenue). It is a mid-cycle figure: above the FY2025 trough because price-band floors keep gross margins above past peaks [Q-9], and below the peak because capex intensity normalizes upward in a downturn. Code reports the terminal share of EV at about 55%, under the 80% watch level.
rationales.peers: INTC, AMAT, LRCX, KLAC. Micron is a capital-intensive, fab-owning memory manufacturer, and the covered/comps universe has no other memory maker. INTC is the only other integrated device manufacturer with owned fabs and heavy capex. AMAT, LRCX and KLAC are wafer-fab-equipment suppliers whose revenue is driven by the same memory/foundry capex cycle (LRCX in particular is memory-heavy), so their multiples carry similar cycle risk. Excluded: fabless/IP and AI-accelerator or connectivity names (NVDA, AMD, AVGO, MRVL, ALAB, CRDO, MPWR), because their asset-light models and growth profiles earn structurally higher, less cyclical multiples. EDA software (SNPS, CDNS) is excluded because it has recurring software economics. Peer TTM ends 2026-06-27 to 2026-07-26 (CY2026Q2) against Micron's 2026-09-03; all are within the 120-day alignment gate. Caveat: none of these peers is a memory maker, so the median EV/Sales (about 15.1x at cutoff closes) has no adjustment for memory's lower through-cycle margins.
rationales.dcf_weight: 0.75 DCF / 0.25 peer EV/Sales. The DCF explicitly models the guided next-four-quarter ramp and a cycle normalization. The EV/Sales cross-check is weak for Micron in two opposing ways. (1) Micron's TTM revenue ($133.2B) understates its current run-rate, since FY2026Q4 alone was $54.2B, which biases relative value down. (2) The peers are not memory makers, and their multiples reflect less cyclical margin structures, which biases it up. Because neither bias can be quantified from the snapshot, the multiple gets a minority weight as a market-based check rather than a primary method. The weight was set before seeing the resulting target price.
